MSC 100.name: Freshman Concert
MSC 100.description: Concert project presenting works from fall and spring semesters. Event arranged and held by students.

MSC 101.name: Department Seminar I
MSC 101.description: Organized with the contribution of faculty, students, guest speakers to aid students in developing skills on verbalizing music, following current trends in composition, learning to approach music from different perspectives, getting to meet living composers and hear them talk about their own music.

MSC 102.name: Department Seminar II
MSC 102.description: Organized with the contribution of faculty, students, guest speakers to aid students in developing skills on verbalizing music, following current trends in composition, learning to approach music from different perspectives, getting to meet living composers and hear them talk about their own music.

MSC 103.name: Symphony Orchestra I
MSC 103.description: Compulsory performance course for all undergraduate students. Bilkent Youth Symphony Orchestra for instrument performance majors. Chorus for voice, composition and piano majors. Youth ensemble open to all majors and possibly offered on event project basis. Western classical music repertoire from Baroque to contemporary.

MSC 104.name: Symphony Orchestra II
MSC 104.description: Compulsory performance course for all undergraduate students. Bilkent Youth Symphony Orchestra for instrument performance majors. Chorus for voice, composition and piano majors. Youth ensemble open to all majors and possibly offered on event project basis. Western classical music repertoire from Baroque to contemporary.

MSC 105.name: Ear Training for Non-Majors I
MSC 105.description: Fundamental properties of sound, elementary acoustics. Basic structural elements of music. Music notation: time and pitch, rhythm, meter, tempo, musical time, staff, solfege syllables, accidentals. Designation of pitch, duration, tempo, expressions and dynamics. Intervals and scales. Methods of musical dictation: Basic reading skills. One part solo solfege.

MSC 106.name: Ear Training for Non-Majors II
MSC 106.description: Chords. Designation of chords. Written and aural exercises on these subjects. Dictation of two period one-part, two-part 16 measures dictees containing mixed rhythms, syncopation. Introduction to collective solfege. The solo and collective musical reading.

MSC 107.name: Individual Music Studies
MSC 107.description: To aid the multi-disciplinary education aim of the University, the instrument courses are offered to all non-majors as elective courses. Students wishing to enroll go through an admission process in which their music abilities are examined. The course is offered for various instruments including flute, clarinet, trumpet and trombone.

MSC 108.name: Individual Music Studies II
MSC 108.description: To aid the multi-disciplinary education aim of the University, the instrument courses are offered to all non-majors as elective courses. Students wishing to enroll go through an admission process in which their music abilities are examined. The course is offered for various instruments including flute, clarinet, trumpet and trombone.

MSC 110.name: The Culture and Basics of Music Making
MSC 110.description: The Culture and Basics of Music Making focuses on the definitions, compositional techniques, performance practices and the structural materials of the music's foremost genres. The course offers a broad perspective that features an eclectic scope of distinct historical and cultural contexts in order to convey a core comprehension of the fundaments of music making process. Many different styles will be discussed including but not limited to: Classical Music, pop music, jazz, funk, electronic music, song, concerto, opera, madrigal, symphony, ballet.

MSC 111.name: Composition I
MSC 111.description: Introduction to composition. Single musical idea applications for choices of solo instruments. Composition dossier consisting of pieces with total duration no less than 5 minutes. Students expected to analyze their works before a jury at the final examination.

MSC 112.name: Composition II
MSC 112.description: Compositions for small-scale chamber music ensembles such as duos or trios. Introduction to composing contrasting material from single musical ideas. Dossier of pieces with total duration no less than 5 minutes. Students are expected to analyze their works before a jury at the final examination.

MSC 113.name: Notation
MSC 113.description: A detailed overview of conventional and contemporary notational techniques, writing idiomatically for instruments.

MSC 114.name: Instrumentation
MSC 114.description: Orchestrational styles and techniques of the 18th and early 19th centuries. Representative scores from the literature and assignments in scoring for various instrumental ensembles.

MSC 121.name: Fundamentals of Musicianship I
MSC 121.description: MSC 121 is available for music majors who need additional background in fundamentals before beginning the theory and history sequence. Improvement of aural skills and musicianship skills will be achieved through the following activities: solfeggio, sight singing, rhythmic reading, melodic dictation, rhythmic dictation, harmonic hearing , error detection.

MSC 122.name: Fundamentals of Musicianship II
MSC 122.description: MSC 122 is available for music majors who need additional background in fundamentals before beginning the theory and history sequence. Improvement of aural skills and musicianship skills will be achieved through the following activities: solfeggio, sight singing, rhythmic reading, melodic dictation, rhythmic dictation, harmonic hearing , error detection.

MSC 131.name: Instrument I
MSC 131.description: Basic principles of professional interpretation through the establishment of professional study techniques. Selected repertoire listing to be performed progressively throughout the semester.

MSC 132.name: Instrument II
MSC 132.description: The continuation of further studies on a new repertoire with the aim to achieve the artistic-technical goals presented in MSC 131.

MSC 133.name: Chamber Music I
MSC 133.description: Score analysis, discussion and study of various composers' principal chamber works. Comparison of formal characteristics, scoring, and compositional practices. Performance of the repertoire consisting of baroque to pre-classic era with particular emphasis on the works of Boccherini, Hummel and Stamitz with various chamber ensembles consisting of various instruments.

MSC 134.name: Chamber Music II
MSC 134.description: Analysis and application of the interpretative styles of the selected repertoire. Practices on the selected repertoire towards achieving unity and balance in performance. Pre-classic to classic repertoire consisting mainly of Haydn's early quartets, trios and Beethoven's duo and trios.

MSC 150.name: Singing for Theatre I
MSC 150.description: Basic singing techniques for theater majors, voice exercises and intonation studies.

MSC 151.name: Singing Voice I
MSC 151.description: Basic principles of professional interpretation through the establishment of professional study techniques. Selected repertoire listing to be performed progressively throughout the semester.

MSC 152.name: Singing Voice II
MSC 152.description: The continuation of further studies on a new repertoire with the aim to achieve the artistic-technical goals presented in MSC 151.

MSC 153.name: Bilkent Chorale I
MSC 153.description: This choir course is designed for all students. Students explore vocal technique, choral singing tone, sight-reading and performance techniques. Students are required to attend all concerts and rehearsals.

MSC 154.name: Bilkent Chorale II
MSC 154.description: Continuation of MSC 153. The course is designed for all students. Students explore vocal technique, choral singing tone, sight-reading and performance techniques. Students are required to attend all concerts and rehearsals.

MSC 155.name: Diction for Singers: English and Italian
MSC 155.description: This course teaches the fundamentals of the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) as it applies to lyrical rules of pronunciation in Italian and English languages.

MSC 156.name: Diction for Singers German/ French
MSC 156.description: This course teaches the fundamentals of the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) as it applies to lyrical rules of pronunciation in German and French languages.

MSC 171.name: Theory I: Fundamentals
MSC 171.description: Fundamentals of music theory: elements of pitch and rhythm, triads and seventh chords, chord-labeling. Fundamentals of voice-leading and consonant harmony: principles of voice-leading, part-writing for triads in root-position and inversion, harmonic progression and the sequence. Cadences, small formal units, and non-chord-tones.

MSC 172.name: Theory II: Harmony and Voice Leading
MSC 172.description: Dissonant harmony: the dominant seventh chord and other types of seventh chords in context, secondary functions and modulation. Harmonic analysis of Bach chorales. Overview of larger forms. Chromaticism: mode mixture and the Neapolitan, augmented-sixth chords, enharmonicism. Further elements of harmonic vocabulary: substitution, alteration, dominant ninth chord, common-tone diminished seventh chord, elements of post-romantic vocabulary and beyond, etc.

MSC 173.name: Origins of Western Music: From Antiquities to Baroque
MSC 173.description: A general view of the content and frontiers of different periods in Western Music History. Music in Antiquity. Roman Liturgy. The genesis of polyphony. Ars nova. Ars subtilior. Burgundy in the Fifteenth Century. Franco-Flemish Composers. Reformation. Instrumental music during the age of Renaissance.

MSC 174.name: Opera and Instrumental Music in the Baroque Period
MSC 174.description: Florentine Camerata. Birth of Opera. Early Baroque vocal music genres. Early Baroque instrumental music genres. Monteverdi Operas. Opera in Rome, Venice and Naples in seventeenth century. Development of keyboard music in the late seventeenth century. The evolution of sonata. Genesis of Orchestral Music during the late seventeenth century. The evolution of concerto.

MSC 181.name: Ear Training I
MSC 181.description: Music notation: time and pitch, rhythm, meter, tempo, musical time, staff, solfege syllables, accidentals. Designation of pitch, duration, tempo, expressions and dynamics. Intervals, scales and modes. Polyphonic and harmonic approach. Chords. Dictation exercises.

MSC 182.name: Ear Training II
MSC 182.description: Tonal functions. Style, phrasing and articulation, abbreviations. Basic triads and their inversions. Seventh chords and their inversions. Ninth chords. Modulation. Secondary degrees. Melody writing. Cadences. Transposition. Written and aural exercises on these subjects. Dictation exercises. Clefs.

MSC 183.name: Keyboard Skills I
MSC 183.description: Basic to intermediate skills of piano playing. Piano as an auxiliary instrument. Sight reading at the piano. Basic methods of realization as defined by O. Gartenlaub. Selected repertoire listing to be performed progressively throughout the semesters.

MSC 184.name: Keyboard Skills II
MSC 184.description: Further study to enhance the skills gained in MSC 183 on a new repertoire.

MSC 185.name: Piano Pedagogy I
MSC 185.description: Fundamentals of piano teaching, examination of the learning process and its application to the elementary student. Hands-on practice and learning in the realm of instruction. Students will observe, teach other pupils, and examine the unique aspects of critique and analysis in the art of pedagogy.

MSC 200.name: Career and Professional Development for Musicians
MSC 200.description: Enhancing "background" aspects of music careers: focusing beyond performance skills. Five modules: Career Portfolio, Concert Programming, AI/Computer Tools, Recording & Post-production, Community Outreach. Topics include audition processes, CVs/resumes, grant applications, concert planning, social media, and recording techniques. Emphasis on building a comprehensive professional portfolio ready for job applications. Each module contributes uniquely to the final portfolio, ensuring a well-rounded professional skillset. Hands-on sessions provide individual feedback, guiding students towards a polished and market-ready portfolio.

MSC 201.name: Department Seminar III
MSC 201.description: Organized with the contribution of faculty, students, guest speakers to aid students in developing skills on verbalizing music, following current trends in composition, learning to approach music from different perspectives, getting to meet living composers and hear them talk about their own music.

MSC 202.name: Department Seminar IV
MSC 202.description: Organized with the contribution of faculty, students, guest speakers to aid students in developing skills on verbalizing music, following current trends in composition, learning to approach music from different perspectives, getting to meet living composers and hear them talk about their own music.

MSC 203.name: Symphony Orchestra III
MSC 203.description: Compulsory performance course for all undergraduate students. Bilkent Youth Symphony Orchestra for instrument performance majors. Chorus for voice, composition and piano majors. Youth ensemble open to all majors and possibly offered on event project basis. Western classical music repertoire from Baroque to contemporary.

MSC 204.name: Symphony Orchestra IV
MSC 204.description: Compulsory performance course for all undergraduate students. Bilkent Youth Symphony Orchestra for instrument performance majors. Chorus for voice, composition and piano majors. Youth ensemble open to all majors and possibly offered on event project basis. Western classical music repertoire from Baroque to contemporary.

MSC 207.name: Individual Music Studies III
MSC 207.description: To aid the multi-disciplinary education aim of the University, the instrument courses are offered to all non-majors as elective courses. Students wishing to enroll go through an admission process in which their music abilities are examined. The course is offered for various instruments including flute, clarinet, trumpet and trombone.

MSC 208.name: Individual Music Studies IV
MSC 208.description: To aid the multi-disciplinary education aim of the University, the instrument courses are offered to all non-majors as elective courses. Students wishing to enroll go through an admission process in which their music abilities are examined. The course is offered for various instruments including flute, clarinet, trumpet and trombone.

MSC 211.name: Composition III
MSC 211.description: Composition for small-scale chamber music ensembles such as quartets. Analysis of similar structures from a broad chronology corresponding with own work. Dossier including completed works of contrasting and related musical ideas with total duration no less than 7 minutes. Students expected to defend their works at the final jury in terms of intellectual approach, composition technique, orchestration, style, form and related criteria.

MSC 212.name: Composition IV
MSC 212.description: Composition for large-scale chamber music ensembles of at least five musicians. Dossier including completed works of at least one single movement with total duration no less than 10 minutes. Students are expected to defend their works at the final jury in terms of intellectual approach, composition technique, orchestration, style, form and related criteria.

MSC 213.name: Orchestration
MSC 213.description: Advanced topics in orchestration focusing on 19th century techniques and conventions.

MSC 214.name: Advanced Orchestration
MSC 214.description: Advanced topics in orchestration focusing on 20th century techniques and conventions.

MSC 231.name: Instrument III
MSC 231.description: Focusing on musicality and mechanical facilities. Comprehension of compositional procedures. Selected repertoire listing to be performed progressively throughout the semester.

MSC 232.name: Instrument IV
MSC 232.description: The continuation of further studies on a new repertoire with the aim to achieve the artistic-technical goals presented in MSC 231.

MSC 233.name: Chamber Music III
MSC 233.description: Performance of the classic era repertoire consisting of works by Beethoven, Mozart and Schubert. Group study on the pieces towards achieving professionalism in the technique of ensemble playing.

MSC 234.name: Chamber Music IV
MSC 234.description: Performance of the classic era repertoire consisting of works by Schubert and Beethoven. Group study on the pieces towards achieving brilliance in balance and unity of the ensemble.

MSC 250.name: Singing for Theatre II
MSC 250.description: Continuation of Singing Theater I, advanced singing techniques for theater majors.

MSC 251.name: Singing Voice III
MSC 251.description: Focusing on musicality and mechanical facilities. Comprehension of compositional procedures. Selected repertoire listing to be performed progressively throughout the semester.

MSC 252.name: Singing Voice IV
MSC 252.description: The continuation of further studies on a new repertoire with the aim to achieve the artistic-technical goals presented in MSC 251.

MSC 253.name: Bilkent Chorale III
MSC 253.description: This choir course is designed for all students. Students explore vocal technique, choral singing tone, sight-reading and performance techniques. Students are required to attend all concerts and rehearsals.

MSC 254.name: Bilkent Chorale IV
MSC 254.description: The course is designed for all students. Students explore vocal technique, choral singing tone, sight-reading and performance techniques. Students are required to attend all concerts and rehearsals.

MSC 255.name: Vocal Literature American/English/Italian
MSC 255.description: This course covers solo vocal literature from prominent Italian, English, and American composers.

MSC 256.name: Vocal Literature German/French
MSC 256.description: This course covers solo vocal literature from prominent German and French composers.

MSC 257.name: Opera Studio I
MSC 257.description: Performance-based studio course for undergraduate voice majors simulating the collaborative environment of operatic production. Preparation and performance of semi-staged opera scenes from contrasting periods of the Western operatic repertoire. Emphasis on stylistic interpretation, ensemble work, stagecraft, memorization, and professional rehearsal practice within a collaborative performance setting.

MSC 258.name: Opera Studio II
MSC 258.description: Preparation and performance of a staged opera scenes program. Emphasis on ensemble coordination, advanced staging, and integration of musical and dramatic elements. Includes an intensive rehearsal process culminating in dress rehearsals and public performance.

MSC 271.name: Theory III: Modal Counterpoint
MSC 271.description: Sixteenth century polyphony with a module for harmony review. Advanced chromatic harmony: bass and soprano harmonization with larger and more difficult examples, review of chromaticism, enharmonicism, and alteration in more diversified and complex environments. Counterpoint: two-and three-part species and free counterpoint, imitation.

MSC 272.name: Theory IV: Classical Form
MSC 272.description: Instrumental forms in Classical Style with a short introduction to twentieth century music. Form and analysis: some contrapuntal forms and the fugue. Formal elements in the instrumental music of the classical era. Tight-knit themes, looser formal regions, full-movement forms such as sonata form, slow-movement forms, minuet/trio form, rondo forms, and concerto form. Some vocal forms and the lied. Ostinato forms, variations, suite. Overview on the practices of twentieth century music: new techniques and materials, post-tonal theory.

MSC 273.name: Music in Europe during the Age of the Enlightenment
MSC 273.description: Handel. Rameau. J.S.Bach. The age of enlightenment and early classical period. Italian Opera Buffa in the early classical period. Opera Seria. Gluck and the opera reform. Haydn. Mozart.

MSC 274.name: 19th Century Music and Modernity
MSC 274.description: Beethoven. Opera trends in the early nineteenth century. Hector Berlioz. Chamber and orchestral musical innovations of the nineteenth century. Nineteenth century Italian Opera. Verdi Operas. Birth of romantic German Opera. Richard Wagner. The German, Austrian and French composers of the late nineteenth century. French naturalism in Opera. Verismo opera. Nationalism in music and its new trends during late nineteenth century. Debussy.

MSC 281.name: Ear Training III
MSC 281.description: Altered chords and chromaticism. Diatonic and chromatic modulation to relative and remote keys. Developing reading skills. Mixed clefs.

MSC 282.name: Ear Training IV
MSC 282.description: Advanced dictation exercises. Advanced ear training for chromatic harmony and polyphony. Advanced reading skills.

MSC 283.name: Keyboard Skills III
MSC 283.description: Progress of the skills acquired in the previous year. Progress of technique. The use of piano as an auxiliary instrument. Selected repertoire listing to be performed progressively throughout the semester.

MSC 284.name: Keyboard Skills IV
MSC 284.description: Basic to intermediate skills of piano playing. Piano as an auxiliary instrument. Sight reading at the piano. Basic methods of realization as defined by O. Gartenlaub. Selected repertoire listing to be performed progressively throughout the semesters.

MSC 300.name: Junior Concert
MSC 300.description: A yearly recital project for the Instrument and Singing option students.

MSC 301.name: Department Seminar V
MSC 301.description: Organized with the contribution of faculty, students, guest speakers to aid students in developing skills on verbalizing music, following current trends in composition, learning to approach music from different perspectives, getting to meet living composers and hear them talk about their own music.

MSC 302.name: Department Seminar VI
MSC 302.description: Organized with the contribution of faculty, students, guest speakers to aid students in developing skills on verbalizing music, following current trends in composition, learning to approach music from different perspectives, getting to meet living composers and hear them talk about their own music.

MSC 303.name: Symphony Orchestra V
MSC 303.description: Compulsory performance course for all undergraduate students. Bilkent Youth Symphony Orchestra for instrument performance majors. Chorus for voice, composition and piano majors. Youth ensemble open to all majors and possibly offered on event project basis. Western classical music repertoire from Baroque to contemporary.

MSC 304.name: Symphony Orchestra VI
MSC 304.description: Compulsory performance course for all undergraduate students. Bilkent Youth Symphony Orchestra for instrument performance majors. Chorus for voice, composition and piano majors. Youth ensemble open to all majors and possibly offered on event project basis. Western classical music repertoire from Baroque to contemporary.

MSC 311.name: Composition V
MSC 311.description: Vocal music composition and/or large chamber music ensemble consisting of at least eight musicians. Analysis of similar structures from a broad chronology corresponding with own work as well as current trends in composition. Dossier including completed work(s) with total duration no less than 15 minutes. Students are expected to defend their works at the final jury in terms of intellectual approach, composition technique, orchestration, style, form and related criteria.

MSC 312.name: Composition VI
MSC 312.description: As the core of composition studies in general becomes apparent at this stage, composition for large-scale music ensembles with an emphasis on achieving own original musical language is expected. Dossier including completed work(s) promising genuine original musical language with total duration no less than 15 minutes. Students are expected to defend their works at the final jury in terms of intellectual approach, composition technique, orchestration, style, form and related criteria as well as own musical language.

MSC 315.name: Score Reading I
MSC 315.description: Introduction to score notion and its realization. Ancient clefs. Transposition. Realization of two part music with ancient clefs and transposing instruments. Musical texture. Sight reading music with more than two parts. Realization of easy to moderate difficulty scores with three and four parts with ancient clefs and transposing instruments where only up to two different transposing instruments co-exist. Realization of simple chamber music scores up to four parts.

MSC 316.name: Score Reading II
MSC 316.description: Identifying musical lines in scores with various textures. Realization of music with four parts with crossing parts. Extended sight reading of repertoire examples up to moderate difficulty with five parts. Sight reading of multiple transposing instruments. Examples from brass and wind parts from late romantic works where at least three different transposing instruments co-exist. Transferring string ensemble textures to keyboard. Realization of scores with strings and up to two transposing parts.

MSC 321.name: Tonal Counterpoint
MSC 321.description: Contrapuntal practices of the Baroque era, with special emphasis on imitation techniques and the "Art of Fugue". The style of J. S. Bach, his predecessors, contemporaries, and followers. Regular assignments, including composition exercises, as well as the analysis of short compositions in the related styles are compulsory.

MSC 322.name: Post - Tonal Theory
MSC 322.description: In-depth survey of compositional styles and techniques of the first half of the 20th century. Traditional pitch-centered analysis, including set theory, as well as approaches focusing on rhythm, timbre, texture, and other elements. Concepts developed through intensive analysis and model compositions.

MSC 323.name: Theory and Analysis of Sonata Forms
MSC 323.description: Focus on the Classical style: Haydn, Mozart, Beethoven. A development of skills in analytical writing in music and a critical assessment of two analytical methodologies pertaining to sonata form: Hepokoski and Darcy's Sonata Theory and William Caplin's Formal Functions. Concepts developed through analysis and model composition.

MSC 324.name: Form and Chromatic Harmony in 19th Century Music
MSC 324.description: Exploration of chromatic harmony in 19th-century instrumental and vocal forms. Developments of sonata form after Beethoven. Concepts developed through analysis and model compositions.

MSC 326.name: Conducting I
MSC 326.description: Brief history of conducting. Posture, stance, movement, breath and primary gestures. Practical choral conducting techniques. Beating patterns of basic meters, with the hand and neutral, legato and light staccato variants. The preparatory beat. The hold and fermata. Starts and cues on all beats and off-beats. Tempo. Continuity. Conducting a chorale. Complex beating patterns, variants, starts, holds, cues. Advanced conducting techniques. Balance and expression. Expressive conducting. Basic analysis. Dealing with voices. Basic vocal techniques. Basic rehearsal techniques. Conducting a madrigal. Conducting plainchant. Soloists. Stage performance. Selected repertoire to be conducted and sight played at the piano.

MSC 331.name: Instrument V
MSC 331.description: High level of musicality and technique in interpretation. Selected repertoire listing to be performed progressively throughout the semester.

MSC 332.name: Instrument VI
MSC 332.description: The continuation of further studies on a new repertoire with the aim to achieve the artistic-technical goals presented in MSC 331.

MSC 333.name: Chamber Music V
MSC 333.description: Performance of the early romantic era repertoire consisting of works by Schubert, Schumann and Mendelssohn.

MSC 334.name: Chamber Music VI
MSC 334.description: Analytic analysis of the repertoire and interpretation styles of the romantic and contemporary chamber music repertoire. Brahms's chamber compositions.

MSC 351.name: Singing Voice V
MSC 351.description: High level of musicality and technique in interpretation. Selected repertoire listing to be performed progressively throughout the semester.

MSC 352.name: Singing Voice VI
MSC 352.description: The continuation of further studies on a new repertoire with the aim to achieve the artistic-technical goals presented in MSC 351.

MSC 353.name: Bilkent Chorale V
MSC 353.description: This choir course is designed for all students. Students explore vocal technique, choral singing tone, sight-reading and performance techniques. Students are required to attend all concerts and rehearsals.

MSC 354.name: Bilkent Chorale VI
MSC 354.description: The course is designed for all students. Students explore vocal technique, choral singing tone, sight-reading and performance techniques. Students are required to attend all concerts and rehearsals.

MSC 355.name: Pedagogy I : Anatomy of the Voice
MSC 355.description: Anatomy of the Voice covers the anatomical, physiological, and acoustical elements of the vocal mechanism and how these components impact singing and vocal health.

MSC 356.name: Pedagogy II: Technique Applications
MSC 356.description: This course explores various vocal pedagogical methods and their applications regarding style.

MSC 373.name: History of 20th Century Music
MSC 373.description: Mahler and Strauss in comparison. Igor Stravinsky. Post-modernism. Atonality. Serialism. Neo-classicism. Integral serialism. Indeterminacy. Timbre. Minimalism. Spectral music.

MSC 374.name: Traditional Turkish Music and Divan Music
MSC 374.description: Social, historical and stylistic background of Classical Turkish Music. Basic elements of musical discourse. Makam, usul, sacred and secular forms, mesk and oral transmission, edvars and the traditional notion of music theory, instruments, instrumental ensembles, vocal traditions. Discussions regarding the classical style and the social change. Some problematic frameworks: periodization of Classical Turkish Music, westernization and/or modernization, orientalism, nationalism, culture politics, ethnomusicology and anthropology, globalization. Problem of musical modernism and traditional resources, interaction between Classical and New Turkish Music and other contemporary/international styles.

MSC 383.name: Keyboard Skills V
MSC 383.description: Applied studies on string, wind, brass and percussion instruments. Basic skills of performance mechanics. Extended information on the instrument and its capabilities. Selected repertoire listing to be performed progressively throughout the semesters.

MSC 384.name: Keyboard Skills VI
MSC 384.description: Applied studies on string, wind, brass and percussion instruments. Basic skills of performance mechanics. Extended information on the instrument and its capabilities. Selected repertoire listing to be performed progressively throughout the semesters.

MSC 386.name: Introduction to Composition
MSC 386.description: For students with little or no previous experience in composition. Exploration of ways of thinking about and organizing basic material elements such as melody, harmony, rhythm and timbre, as well as developing skills of score preparation and analytical listening. Exposition to a variety of ideas and techniques, based very broadly on Western "art" music of the 20th century, but not attempting to guide towards any particular style. The primary emphasis on process of learning through feedback, via individual and group meetings as well as frequent opportunities to hear compositional exercises performed and recorded.

MSC 399.name: Summer Practice
MSC 399.description: Minimum 6 weeks practice at music related institutions.

MSC 400.name: Senior Concert
MSC 400.description: A dossier consisting of all works presented in the composition course juries must include music for solo instruments, small and large-scale chamber ensembles, vocal music and orchestral music. The dossier including works totaling no less than one hour should be presented to the jury 10 working days prior to the graduation project concert. The composition student must organize a concert covering selection of his compositions.

MSC 401.name: Department Seminar VII
MSC 401.description: Organized with the contribution of faculty, students, guest speakers to aid students in developing skills on verbalizing music, following current trends in composition, learning to approach music from different perspectives, getting to meet living composers and hear them talk about their own music.

MSC 402.name: Department Seminar VIII
MSC 402.description: Organized with the contribution of faculty, students, guest speakers to aid students in developing skills on verbalizing music, following current trends in composition, learning to approach music from different perspectives, getting to meet living composers and hear them talk about their own music.

MSC 403.name: Symphony Orchestra VII
MSC 403.description: Compulsory performance course for all undergraduate students. Bilkent Youth Symphony Orchestra for instrument performance majors. Chorus for voice, composition and piano majors. Youth ensemble open to all majors and possibly offered on event project basis. Western classical music repertoire from Baroque to contemporary.

MSC 404.name: Symphony Orchestra VIII
MSC 404.description: Compulsory performance course for all undergraduate students. Bilkent Youth Symphony Orchestra for instrument performance majors. Chorus for voice, composition and piano majors. Youth ensemble open to all majors and possibly offered on event project basis. Western classical music repertoire from Baroque to contemporary.

MSC 411.name: Composition VII
MSC 411.description: Composition of a large-scale genuinely creative work for orchestra. Dossier of advanced sketches including orchestral fragments of work in progress. Students expected to present thorough domination on their work and use appropriate technical jargon while they defend their work at the final jury in terms of intellectual approach, composition technique, orchestration, style, form and related criteria as well as own musical language.

MSC 412.name: Composition VIII: Graduation Project
MSC 412.description: The work submitted at the final jury of composition vii should be completed. The work should portray originality and advanced skills on compositional technique, form and orchestration. Students are expected to present thorough domination on their work and use appropriate technical jargon while they defend their work at the final jury in terms of intellectual approach, composition technique, orchestration, style, form and related criteria as well as own musical language.

MSC 415.name: Score Reading III
MSC 415.description: Realization of full scores up to late romantic period. Emphasis on developments in orchestration in the romantic period. Orchestral texture, timbre, balance and aural expectancy. Omission of orchestral doublings in piano realization and voice leading according to hand position. Textural transfer and playing a full score on piano. Applications on transcription.

MSC 416.name: Score Reading IV
MSC 416.description: Realization of advanced full scores starting from late romantic period. Extended information on orchestral texture, timbre, sound balance and aural expectancy. Executing modern scores with extended technique on the piano. Transcriptions and prima vista practices.

MSC 421.name: Theory and Analysis of Contemporary Music
MSC 421.description: In-depth survey of compositional styles and techniques of the second half of the 20th century. Topics of Post-serialism, New Complexity, Spectralism, Musique Concrete Instrumental, Micropolyphony, Aleatoric music, Chance music, Stochastic music and also more recent developments.

MSC 425.name: Conducting II
MSC 425.description: The baton. Basic beating patterns with the baton. Practical conducting techniques using the baton in all meters with neutral, legato and light staccato variants. The expressive hand. Conducting a string orchestra. Selected repertoire to be conducted and sight played on the piano. Methods of preparatory study. Rehearsal planning. Advanced beating patterns with the baton, combining meters. Dealing with solo passages.] Improvement of manual skills. Flow of movement. Methods on eye contact. Balance. The rehearsal versus the performance. Conducting a classical orchestra. Known intricacies of some important orchestral passages. Fundamentals of performance psychology on stage. Vocal versus instrumental. The soloist and accompaniment. Further study of rehearsal planning. Analysis of conducting styles. Concert and program planning. Selected repertoire to be conducted and sight played on the piano.

MSC 426.name: Conducting III
MSC 426.description: Conductor as a performer. Expressive gestures implying qualities of sound and silence. Performance gestures of dynamics, kinetics, agogics. Transitions of time beating gestures and expressive gestures. Comparative discussions of schools of N. Malko and I. Music on conducting performance technique.

MSC 427.name: Conducting IV
MSC 427.description: Conductor as interpreter. Interpretative analysis. Analysis of work and choice of gestures. Interpretative aural imagination, its application. Completion and molding of conducting gesture techniques including unmetrical gestures. Planning timing and conducting the rehearsal week and the performance.

MSC 431.name: Instrument VII
MSC 431.description: Maturity in every aspect of interpretation. Analysis of style and interpretation on pieces. Selected repertoire listing to be performed progressively throughout the semester.

MSC 432.name: Instrument VIII: Graduation Concert
MSC 432.description: The continuation of further studies on a new repertoire with the aim to achieve the artistic-technical goals presented in MSC 431. Preparation and rehearsal of the graduation repertoire also including a must piece that is chosen by the graduation jury and submitted to each student two weeks prior to the graduation concert.

MSC 433.name: Chamber Music VII
MSC 433.description: Introduction to the chamber music compositions of Turkish Composers. Beethoven's late quartets. Study and practices with the aim of achieving maturity in stage performance.

MSC 434.name: Chamber Music VIII
MSC 434.description: Analytic analysis and interpretation of the contemporary chamber music repertoire consisting of compositions by Dvorak, Shostakovich, Ravel, Debussy, Webern, Bartok, Saygun, Erkin.

MSC 451.name: Singing Voice VII
MSC 451.description: Maturity in every aspect of interpretation. Analysis of style and interpretation on pieces. Selected repertoire listing to be performed progressively throughout the semester.

MSC 452.name: Singing VIII: Graduation Concert
MSC 452.description: The continuation of further studies on a new repertoire with the aim to achieve the artistic-technical goals presented in MSC 451. Preparation and rehearsal of the graduation repertoire also including a must piece that is chosen by the graduation jury and submitted to each student two weeks prior to the graduation concert.

MSC 453.name: Bilkent Chorale VII
MSC 453.description: This choir course is designed for all students. Students explore vocal technique, choral singing tone, sight-reading and performance techniques. Students are required to attend all concerts and rehearsals.

MSC 454.name: Bilkent Chorale VIII
MSC 454.description: The course is designed for all students. Students explore vocal technique, choral singing tone, sight-reading and performance techniques. Students are required to attend all concerts and rehearsals.

MSC 459.name: Opera Studies V
MSC 459.description: Major works of opera repertoire performed.

MSC 460.name: Opera Studies VI
MSC 460.description: Cornerstone works of opera repertoire are performed.

MSC 470.name: Career and Professional Development for Musicians
MSC 470.description: Enhancing "background" aspects of music careers: focusing beyond performance skills. Five modules: Career Portfolio, Concert Programming, AI/Computer Tools, Recording & Post-production, Community Outreach. Topics include audition processes, CVs/resumes, grant applications, concert planning, social media, and recording techniques. Emphasis on building a comprehensive professional portfolio ready for job applications. Each module contributes uniquely to the final portfolio, ensuring a well-rounded professional skillset. Hands-on sessions provide individual feedback, guiding students towards a polished and market-ready portfolio.

MSC 473.name: Contemporary Turkish Music
MSC 473.description: Sociopolitical, cultural, and stylistic background of New Turkish Music. European influenced music life, its styles and institutionalization in Turkey beginning with the late Ottoman era. Culture politics, statist music institutionalization, polyphonic styles in the early republican and the post-war Turkey. Acting on the fault lines: stylistic polarization among first two composer generations, alaturka-alafranga and monophony-polyphony debates, nationalization-globalization dilemma, battling paradigms of the Turkish-traditional versus the international-modernized.

MSC 474.name: Music of Igor Stravinsky
MSC 474.description: Studies on the Stravinsky's works with consideration of four different periods: Early pieces, Russian Phase, Neo-Classicism and Serialism.

MSC 476.name: Studies on Modality
MSC 476.description: Review of the theory and ear training of modes. Analyzing examples from Machaut, Dufay, Josquin, Greig, Mussorgsky, Debussy, Bartok, Samuel Barber.

MSC 477.name: Contemporary Notational Techniques
MSC 477.description: Does notation reflect the actual composition that we have in mind? How much does music notation affect the actual performance? Can we increase our musical communication skills through notation? A brief historical overview on music notation. Basic notation principles and contemporary notation styles. The course focuses on handwriting skills (no notation software will be used).

MSC 478.name: Source Readings in Music
MSC 478.description: Discussion group based on important writings and speeches in music history from ancient Greece through the twentieth century. Anthological readings on music and musical concepts throughout the ages. Active participation is required.

MSC 479.name: Modern Music Before 1945
MSC 479.description: Music of fin de siecle and pre-war period in Europe and U.S.A. Observation of the artistic and socio-cultural environment of the related period. Samples of a broad spectrum of musical life in the twentieth century, including orchestral, choral, band, chamber music, and solo repertoire, both instrumental and vocal.

MSC 480.name: Modern Music After 1945
MSC 480.description: A socio-historical view on the music of post-war generation in Europe and U.S.A. Focus on the major trends (such as of avant-gardism) and technical developments in music (such as serialism) of the related period.

MSC 481.name: Contemporary Turkish Piano Music
MSC 481.description: General information on the musical styles of Rey, Erkin, Saygun and Akses. Observation on the development of the piano literature among these national composers. Detailed analysis and discussion group on the style and performance of the selected repertoire.

MSC 482.name: Piano Literature
MSC 482.description: Survey of instruments historic development and its repertoire with emphasis on cornerstone works. Comparative listening to master artists' renditions their interpretations and style practices. Building programs for concerts, recitals, recordings, competitions.

MSC 487.name: Introduction to Electroacoustic Music
MSC 487.description: Basic techniques of electroacoustic music composition, including recording, sound editing, synthesis, MIDI, sequencers and sampling. Projects realized using recording gear and computers; study of relevant aspects of acoustic and electronic theory; repertoire since 1948 of musique concrete, acousmatic, and live-electronic music; Hands-on work will culminate in a final performance of individual projects.

MSC 488.name: Interactive Computer Music with Max
MSC 488.description: Hands-on programming and composition course that explores sound design and HCI (human computer interaction) as the ingredients for the creation of engaging real-time interactive musical experiences. Students will learn about the principles, design considerations, and aesthetic qualities of interactive music through the Max environment.

MSC 500.name: Department Seminar
MSC 500.description: Organized with the contribution of faculty, students, guest speakers to aid students in developing skills on verbalizing music, following current trends in composition, learning to approach music from different perspectives, getting to meet living composers and hear them talk about their own music.

MSC 511.name: Music Performance and Interpretation I
MSC 511.description: Individual instruction on repertoire in music performance and interpretation.

MSC 512.name: Conducting I
MSC 512.description: Individual instruction on instrumental and opera repertoire in conducting.

MSC 513.name: Music Composition I
MSC 513.description: Individual instruction on musical composition to prepare original works.

MSC 515.name: Music Theory
MSC 515.description: Musical analysis and writing skills of modal and tonal music subjects are taught individually. Consideration of varied analytical methods of musical analysis and history of music theory from Aristoxenus till Stockhausen on specialized topics determined by faculty. These provide to comprehend various research methods, analytical skills, writing skills and stylistic features of the related era on different perspectives.

MSC 517.name: Tonal Music Topics and Analysis
MSC 517.description: Musical analysis of tonal music in the broadest sense, covering examples from the 17th century to the first decades of the 20th century. Consideration of varied analytical methods of musical analysis, emphasis on Schenkerian and Riemannian approaches on specialized topics determined by the faculty.

MSC 521.name: Master's Lecture Recital
MSC 521.description: Lecture demonstration concert on a topic appropriate to the candidate's major area of specialization.

MSC 525.name: Bilkent Ensembles
MSC 525.description: Students actively participate in concert projects of one or more of Bilkent University's music ensembles such as Bilkent Symphony Orchestra, Bilkent Youth Quartet, Bilkent Chorus and Bilkent Modern Ensemble throughout the academic semester.

MSC 527.name: Masters Theory Presentation
MSC 527.description: Students are expected to finalize and present part or all of their papers stated in MSG 515 at class(es) decided upon with the consent of the student's advisor.

MSC 531.name: Music Performance and Interpretation II
MSC 531.description: Individual instruction on repertoire in music performance and interpretation.

MSC 532.name: Conducting II
MSC 532.description: Individual instruction on instrumental and opera repertoire in conducting.

MSC 533.name: Music Composition II
MSC 533.description: Individual instruction on musical composition to prepare original works.

MSC 535.name: Contemporary Instrumentation and Performance Practice
MSC 535.description: Exploration of ideas in contemporary music performance, in diverse styles, through reading, playing, and writing. In-depth investigation of compositional ideas, playing techniques, approaches to sound, notation, performance venues, and new modes of interaction between composers, performers, and audiences.

MSC 537.name: Studies in History of Western Music
MSC 537.description: Evolution of different musical genres through history. Advanced discussions on the genesis, development and contemporary applications of the specific genres.

MSC 541.name: Master's Final Concert
MSC 541.description: A full-length concert as the culminating requirement for the master's degree.

MSC 550.name: Department Seminar
MSC 550.description: Weekly meetings hosted by faculty with visiting artists, scholars. Master-classes, workshops, presentations focusing on predetermined subjects. Each graduate student also prepares a presentation.

MSC 551.name: Music Performance and Interpretation
MSC 551.description: Studies and practices on performance and interpretation of selected repertoire from all genres and periods involving major field. Course incorporates a wide range of repertoire such as solo, sonata, concerto as well as chamber music, ensembles, orchestral solos and excerpts for instrument performance majors. Lied, complete roles in operas for vocal majors. All choral, ensemble and orchestral repertoire for conducting majors as included in departmental repertoire lists.

MSC 553.name: Music Composition
MSC 553.description: Music composition courses are taught individually. This provides flexibility in adapting to the interest and needs of each student. Composition courses have several purposes: to equip the student with necessary technical skills to develop their musical ideas, to help them get acquainted with the most recent compositional styles, and supply guidance with their projects. Each semester students will produce an original composition, culminating in a portfolio at the end of their Ph.D. studies.

MSC 561.name: Music Performance and Interpretation
MSC 561.description: Studies and practices on performance and interpretation of selected repertoire from all genres and periods involving major field. Course incorporates a wide range of repertoire such as solo, sonata, concerto as well as chamber music, ensembles, orchestral solos and excerpts for instrument performance majors. Lied, complete roles in operas for vocal majors. All choral, ensemble and orchestral repertoire for conducting majors as included in departmental repertoire lists.

MSC 563.name: Music Composition
MSC 563.description: Music composition courses are taught individually. This provides flexibility in adapting to the interest and needs of each student. Composition courses have several purposes: to equip the student with necessary technical skills to develop their musical ideas, to help them get acquainted with the most recent compositional styles, and supply guidance with their projects. Each semester students will produce an original composition, culminating in a portfolio at the end of their Ph.D. studies.

MSC 567.name: New Music Topics and Analysis
MSC 567.description: Musical analysis of post-tonal music from the first half of the 20th century onwards. Concepts such as set theory, serialism, centricity and modality are incorporated.

MSC 568.name: Theoretical Studies in Tonal Music
MSC 568.description: Analysis of music from the tonal repertoire by emphasis on structural aspects of each individual work. With discussions focusing on different analytical perspectives such as formalist methods, hermeneutics, phenomenology, Neo-Riemannian and cultural studies.

MSC 569.name: History of Tonal Music Theory
MSC 569.description: From Rameau to beyond: This course will examine different scale-degree and functional approaches to tonal harmony, discussion of seminal theoretical texts (Rameau, Sechter, Riemann, Schenker etc.), we will work on comparative music analyses to explore different conceptions of harmonic space and their limits.

MSC 570.name: Introduction to Schenkerian Analysis
MSC 570.description: This course provides an introduction to the theories and analytical methods of Heinrich Schenker and his followers through the analysis of selected works.

MSC 571.name: Contextual Perspectives in History of Western Music

MSC 577.name: Symphony after Beethoven
MSC 577.description: Beethoven's 9th symphony, from its very first performance on, leads to a complicated reception history. Some major reactions, early and after, can be cited as follows: crisis of symphony in the German speaking culture domain, Berlioz's symphonie fantastique and Liszt's 12 Poemes symphoniques, drame lyrique of Wagner -who considers himself as being brought to "the other side of the red sea" through Beethoven-, music-esthetic considerations like Brendel's Zukunftsmusik and the schism among absolute and programmatic music according to Hanslick, monumental symphonies by Bruckner and Mahler, symphonists and reactions to symphonic forms during the 20th century etc. Essayistic involvement in German and French by some 19th century composers like Schumann, Liszt, Wagner and Berlioz deserves a special attention regarding the problematic. Topics, readings and work selection of course are refreshed as per the specific phenomenon im Visier of current semester.

MSC 578.name: History of Stage Music
MSC 578.description: Stage music after Tristan to our day. An all-embracing historical discourse on the 19th century music disregarding the impact of Wagner's Tristan und Isolde is hard to imagine. Wagner himself, his contemporaries, and following composer generations involved with stage music have thenceforth to grapple with that work and its reception. The design of course regards Wagner's output, before all, as a socio historical demarcation line in the framework of the genre and takes each semester a different single opera or music theater work in hand, or, in some cases, a group of works clustered around a single thematic and/or problematic.

MSC 580.name: Topics in Contemporary Turkish Music
MSC 580.description: Course problematizes the activity of the exterritorial composer. It can be asserted that the western serious music has established itself as the main reference point for other musical domains, peu a peu, after the French Revolution. Course attempts to problematize the self-styled and auto-centralizing qualities of western thought of music on the one hand and discourses of identity of the non-western composers on the other. Considerations of generally extra-musical fields of contemporary social thought and of diverse authors such as Levinas, Adorno, Derrida, Deleuze, oriental and colonial studies, cultural and gender studies etc. are vital part of course. On the empirical side presents New Turkish Music the main subject matter to be tackled.

MSC 581.name: Music Performance and Interpretation
MSC 581.description: Studies and practices on performance and interpretation of selected repertoire from all genres and periods involving major field. Course incorporates a wide range of repertoire such as solo, sonata, concerto as well as chamber music, ensembles, orchestral solos and excerpts for instrument performance majors. Lied, complete roles in operas for vocal majors. All choral, ensemble and orchestral repertoire for conducting majors as included in departmental repertoire lists.

MSC 583.name: Music Composition
MSC 583.description: Music composition courses are taught individually. This provides flexibility in adapting to the interest and needs of each student. Composition courses have several purposes: to equip the student with necessary technical skills to develop their musical ideas, to help them get acquainted with the most recent compositional styles, and supply guidance with their projects. Each semester students will produce an original composition, culminating in a portfolio at the end of their Ph.D. studies.

MSC 584.name: Music of the Last Decade
MSC 584.description: This is a course concentrating on music that is written in the last ten years. The goal of the course is to contextualize recent trends in composition and develop a framework necessary to understand and analyze representative examples from this period.

MSC 585.name: Opera in the 20th Century
MSC 585.description: This is a seminar course examining the 20th century opera repertoire. We will investigate how the opera genre has transformed in the 20th century by looking at works like Pelleas et Melisande, Bluebeard's Castle, Lulu, Saint Francois d'Assise, Le Grand Macabre, Einstein on the Beach, Punch and Judy. We will specifically investigate the conventions that the modern composers have inherited from the past, to reject or re-embrace.

MSC 586.name: Microtonality
MSC 586.description: An in-depth investigation of different microtonal usages and techniques in composition. Topics will range from just intonation to different types of extended equal temperaments. We will also examine different practical strategies developed by composers in writing microtonal music. Each student will compose a piece using techniques covered in class.

MSC 587.name: Advanced Topics in Computer Music
MSC 587.description: Advanced topics in computer music selected from such subjects as: interactivity, algorithmic composition, VR/AR technologies, game audio, sound spatialization, audio programming languages and software design.

MSC 599.name: Master's Thesis
MSC 599.description: A research-based thesis course on an individual project. Timely, relevant and substantial research on a topic in the general area of Music. Topic to be agreed in consultation with a Master Thesis advisor.

MSC 691.name: Doctoral Lecture Concert
MSC 691.description: Students are expected to prepare and perform a major concert. The concert is preceded by a lecture by the student on works to be performed and their interpretation. Students with applied majors in instrument, vocal, conducting, chamber music and composition prepare their lecture concert program proposals with their respective advisers. Students are expected to submit their proposals to the department board prior to registering for the course and course may only be registered to upon the proposal of the advisor to and the final approval by department board of the lecture concert program proposal. Advisor and department board may choose to revise the student's proposal. Doctoral lecture recitals are held open to public. Assessment and grading is done by a jury selected by the department board. Department board may choose to utilize other means of assessment such as review of the performances recordings by peer or professionals in the field.

MSC 695.name: Doctoral Proficiency Concert
MSC 695.description: Students are expected to prepare and perform a major recital and a graduation concert. The recital is preceded by a lecture by the student on works to be performed. Students with applied majors in instrument, vocal, conducting, chamber music and composition prepare their lecture recital and concert program proposals with their respective advisers. Students are expected to submit their proposals to the department board prior to registering for the course and course may only be registered to upon the proposal of the advisor to and the final approval by department board of the lecture concert program proposal. Advisor and department board may choose to revise the student's proposal. Doctoral lecture recitals are held open to public. Assessment and grading is done by a jury selected by the department board. Department board may choose to utilize other means of assessment such as review of the performances recordings by peer or professionals in the field.
MSC 695.prerequisite: (MSC 693 and MSC 581) or ( MSC 693 and MSC 583)

MSC 699.name: Proficiency in Art Graduation Project
MSC 699.description: Graduation project for Proficiency in Art majors. For performance majors: A major performance and a research document on a related subject; For composition majors: A major composition and research document on a related subject.

MSC 931.name: Individual Music Studies V
MSC 931.description: Individual instrumental instruction. Designed specifically for non-music majors. Students should be minimally at the intermediate level of proficiency on their instrument. Substantial practice time and jury exams are required.

MSC 932.name: Individual Music Studies VI
MSC 932.description: Individual instrumental instruction. Designed specifically for non-music majors. Students should be minimally at the intermediate level of proficiency on their instrument. Substantial practice time and jury exams are required.

MSC 941.name: Individual Music Studies VII
MSC 941.description: To aid the multi-disciplinary education aim of the University, the instrument courses are offered to all non-majors as elective courses. Students wishing to enroll go through an admission process in which their music abilities are examined. The course is offered for various instruments including flute, clarinet, trumpet and trombone.

MSC 954.name: Improvisation Ensemble
MSC 954.description: Improvisation Ensemble is a performance-based course. Concepts like silence, gesture, dynamics, phrasing, breathing, timbre, timbral polyphony, holistic listening, internal and external focusing, concentration, pulsation, rhythm, phrasing, articulation, continuity, texture, textural transformation, form, shape are not only discussed but literally experienced. Class participation, performance and weekly assignments.
